findings.title: include_website_name is not a predicate method, so the attribute is always serialized
findings.body: The method is named `include_website_name` (without a trailing `?`), but ActiveModel::Serializers only calls `include_<attr>?` predicate methods to decide whether to include an attribute. Because no `include_website_name?` method exists, the serializer falls back to always including `website_name`. This means `website_name` is serialized even when `website` is blank/nil, producing a JSON payload with `website_name: null` for every user with no website. The guard `website.present?` inside the method is dead code in this context. The method should be renamed to `include_website_name?` (matching the pattern used by `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, etc. in the same file).

findings.title: website_name logic is incorrect for subdomain relationships and can produce wrong display text
findings.body: The `website_name` method attempts to show the full path when the website host matches the instance host, but the branching logic is flawed. In the `elsif` branch (line 144), it compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` with `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` — this strips the first label from both hosts and compares the remainders. For `website_host = 'forums.example.com'` and `discourse_host = 'example.com'`, the lengths differ (3 vs 2) so this branch is skipped, but for `website_host = 'a.b.example.com'` and `discourse_host = 'c.b.example.com'` (both length 4), it would incorrectly treat them as the same site. More importantly, the final `else` branch (line 149) checks `discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)`, which correctly handles `forums.example.com` ending with `.example.com`, but the middle branch's length-equality requirement means cases like `website_host = 'www.example.com'` (3 labels) vs `discourse_host = 'example.com'` (2 labels) fall through to the else branch and are handled correctly only by accident. The logic is convoluted and the comment on line 148 ('example.com == forum.example.com') describes the else branch but the condition actually tests the reverse (instance is subdomain of website). Consider simplifying to a single check: show the path when `website_host == discourse_host || discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)`.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed multiple times in website_name
findings.body: The `website_name` method calls `URI(website.to_s)` three separate times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149) to extract the host and path. Each call re-parses the URL string. This is wasteful — the parsed URI object should be computed once and reused. While the performance impact is negligible for a single serialization, it's called for every user in list views (e.g., user directory, admin user list), so the redundant parsing adds up. Extract `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil` once at the top and use `uri.host` and `uri.path` throughout.

findings.title: Website link uses unescaped href attribute that could allow javascript: URLs
findings.body: The template renders `<a href={{model.website}} ...>` where `model.website` comes directly from user profile data (user-controlled input). While the server-side `website` field is presumably validated on save, the serializer returns the raw `user_profile.website` value without any scheme validation. If a user can set their website to `javascript:alert(1)` (depending on server-side validation in the user profile update path, which is not shown in this PR), clicking the link would execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the Discourse site. The `website_name` display text is safely derived from the host, but the `href` uses the raw URL. The server should enforce http/https scheme on the website field, or the serializer should sanitize it. At minimum, this is a defense-in-depth concern — the href should be validated to start with `http://` or `https://`.

findings.title: Untrusted attributes test does not include website_name, so the TL0/anonymous privacy leak is not caught
findings.body: The test on line 11 defines `untrusted_attributes` as `%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}` but does NOT include `:website_name`. Since `website_name` was added to the `untrusted_attributes` list in the serializer (line 109 of user_serializer.rb), it should be included in this test to verify that TL0 users' website names are hidden from anonymous viewers. Without this, the test passes even if the `untrusted_attributes` mechanism is broken for `website_name`, and a privacy regression (leaking a TL0 user's website path to anonymous users) would go undetected. Additionally, because `include_website_name` is not a proper predicate (see separate finding), the attribute may be serialized even when `website` is blank, which this test also fails to catch.

findings.title: No test for website_name when website is blank or nil
findings.body: The spec only tests `website_name` when a website is filled out (line 67+). There is no test verifying that `website_name` is absent (or null) when `user_profile.website` is blank. Given the `include_website_name` predicate bug (it's not a real predicate), this case is important to test — it would catch the bug where `website_name` is always serialized even for users with no website. A test like `expect(json).not_to have_key(:website_name)` when website is nil would be appropriate.

findings.title: JSDoc comment for profileBackground was incorrectly changed from websiteName
findings.body: The diff changed the JSDoc `@property` annotation from `websiteName` to `profileBackground` on the `profileBackground` computed property. This appears to be an accidental edit — the original `@property websiteName` was already wrong (it should have been `profileBackground` for this method), but the change in this PR is unrelated to the website_name feature. While the fix is technically correct (the doc now matches the method name), it's an unrelated change bundled into this PR. More importantly, the original code had a `websiteName` computed property in the controller (removed in this PR) that had no JSDoc, and this model file never had a `websiteName` property — so the original `@property websiteName` on `profileBackground` was a pre-existing copy-paste error. The fix is correct but should have been a separate commit/PR.
